info.title: Elpis
info.description: The trust layer for autonomous commerce: control, verify, settle, recover. A payment is proposed, judged, and then either staged in a cancellable window, held for a human, or refused. An authorized proposal may stage real escrow immediately. Use the evaluate endpoint for a dry run.

bearerAuth.description: An API key scoped to read, propose and/or approve. A key can only do what its scopes allow; approve is privileged; do not grant it to untrusted agents.

Decision.description: What the treasury decided, and why. The state is the answer, not a status of the request.

id.description: The action id. Read it back with GET /api/v1/actions/{id}.

state.description: STAGED: in escrow and cancellable until window.finalizeAt. APPROVAL_REQUIRED: a person must decide. BLOCKED: a rule refused it and nothing moved — do not retry unchanged.

amount.description: Formatted for a human, e.g. "25.00 USDC".

amountBaseUnits.description: USDC base units (6 decimals), for arithmetic.

recoverabilityClass.description: R1 fully reversible, R2 reversible before finalization, R3 compensatable, R4 irreversible.

summary.description: Plain-language statement of what can still be undone. Written in the conditional until the mechanism is actually in place.

cancellable.description: True only while a live window is open.

gasCostMicro.description: What this settlement cost on chain, in micro-USD. A cost, not a fee.

blockedBy.description: The rules that refused it, with the reason in the reader's language.

code.description: bad_request, unauthorized, forbidden, duplicate, rate_limited, payment_required.

get.summary: Balances, pools, limits, and what is currently cancellable. Start here.
Recent actions with their state and recoverability.

post.summary: Submit a payment proposal; an authorized action may stage real escrow.
post.description: Runs every control and returns STAGED, APPROVAL_REQUIRED or BLOCKED with the reasons. Pass an `idempotency-key` header (or a `reference`) so a retry returns the same action instead of paying twice.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: One key per intent. A retry with the same key cannot create a second payment.

documentRef.description: Required above the treasury's document threshold.

409.description: This idempotency key already produced an action.

get.summary: One action in full. Read it back after a timeout — the money may already be in escrow.

post.summary: Cancel a payment that has not staged yet. A staged payment is settled by its condition instead.
Settle a staged payment against its committed condition. Release on a proof, refund on a problem.
post.description: This replaces recalling a staged payment: the committed condition decides, not the payer. A `proof` that satisfies the condition releases the payment; a `problem` (a genuine contradiction) refunds it. Every settlement records an attestation so the decision can be reproduced.

400.description: Provide a proof to release, or a problem to refund.

409.description: The condition already decided; the payment is final.

post.summary: Dry-run a payment: what would happen, without proposing it.
post.description: Runs every deterministic control — rules, recoverability classification, supervisor and approval — against current state and returns the decision (blocked, held for a human, frozen, or proceed on its own) without persisting an action or moving money. An agent that can ask first is materially safer than one that has to act to find out.

get.summary: Self-serve API key circulation and daily issuance availability.

200.description: Active circulation, remaining slots, and default key limits.

post.summary: Issue a bounded self-serve API key (read + propose) with optional referral attribution.

ref.description: Optional Elpis referral code from another user or AI agent.

201.description: Issued API key, workspace ID, referral code, and starter credit balance.

429.description: Circulation cap or rate limit reached.

post.summary: A human releases a payment that is waiting. Requires the approve scope.
post.description: Deliberately a separate scope: a proposal is not an authorization. An untrusted agent key should not receive the approve scope. Keys granted both scopes have both capabilities.

post.summary: Submit the owner's signed transactions for a self-custodied treasury.
post.description: Every transaction is read back from the chain and matched against the plan the owner was shown — same contract, same calldata — before anything is recorded.

get.summary: The meter: this period's usage, its cost, and the credit balance.

200.description: Usage and pricing for the current period.

get.summary: The self-serve billing view: deposit address, reference, balance and this period's cost.
get.description: Elpis never takes custody. The deposit address is the organization's own treasury address, and a top-up is a transfer to it recorded against the reference this response supplies.

200.description: Balance, deposit instructions, and the current period's usage cost.

post.summary: Commit a settlement job: fix what "done" means before the work begins.
post.description: Persists the committed acceptance condition, binds it to a deadline and returns a commitmentHash. The stored condition is the one that settles — it cannot be rewritten after commit. Pass an `idempotency-key` header (or an `idempotencyKey` body field) so a retry returns the first job instead of committing a second one.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: One key per intent. A retry with the same key cannot create a second job.

provider.description: Who delivers the work — the reputation subject.

condition.description: The acceptance checks. Each is { kind, ...fields }; kinds are deliverable_hash, artifact_in_set, numeric_range, counterparty_signature, document_anchor, oracle_equals, witness_attestation.

deadline.description: The refund horizon — time never releases, it only returns.

201.description: The committed job, with its commitmentHash.

get.summary: List this organization's settlement jobs, newest first.

200.description: A list of jobs, each with claims and how much has released.

get.summary: Read one job: the committed condition, per-check status, decision and attestation.

post.summary: Record delivery evidence against a job without settling it.
post.description: Evidence is bound to the commitment it answers; it settles later via /settle, the deadline, or a refund.

200.description: The job with the evidence recorded.

get.summary: What was submitted, when, and how each committed check currently reads.

200.description: The delivered evidence and its per-check status.

post.summary: Dry-run a proof: what WOULD happen, recording nothing.
post.description: Runs the same pure decision over the committed condition and a candidate proof and returns release / refund / hold without persisting anything. Ask before acting.

200.description: The projected decision and per-check results.

409.description: The condition was altered since commit.

post.summary: The primitive over HTTP — decide a condition and proof, with no account and no persistence.
post.description: Runs the exact commit/settle decision and returns release / refund / hold, the per-check ledger and the reproducible attestation. Writes nothing, moves no money and needs no key: it is the playground's backend and a developer's first call. Rate-limited per address.

condition.description: Acceptance checks, validated against the frozen check vocabulary.

deadline.description: ISO-8601. A passed deadline can only refund, never release.

200.description: The decision, per-check results, commitment hash and attestation.

400.description: Malformed JSON or an invalid condition.

post.summary: Settle the job on its committed condition — release, refund, or hold.
post.description: Release on a proof that satisfies the condition, refund on a contradiction, hold while the proof is missing. The decision and its reproducible attestation are recorded on the job. Pass an `idempotency-key` so a retry after a lost response replays the first answer instead of conflicting with it.

post.summary: Refund the job on demand — the safe direction (money returns, never releases).
Re-run the decision and confirm it reproduces the recorded attestation.

200.description: matches: true when the settlement is a reproducible result.

post.summary: Settle a milestone claim: a cumulative amount, releasing only the delta over the previous claim.
post.description: Each claim id is consumed once — a rejected claim stays consumed, so a milestone can never be double-paid. An `idempotency-key` additionally makes the response itself replayable.

claimId.description: A stable id for this claim; consumed exactly once.

cumulativeAmount.description: Total claimed including this claim, in base units.

201.description: The job, the claim, the delta and how much released.

get.summary: The milestone claims against a job, in order, and how much released.

200.description: The claims and the released total.

post.summary: Open a dispute, freezing automatic settlement until it is resolved.
post.description: A dispute is the escalation path for what the committed predicate cannot see: quality, a challenge to evidence, a delivery that passed its checks but was not what was wanted. While it is open, neither the deadline nor /settle may decide the job. Pass an `idempotency-key` so a retry replays the first response.

evidence.description: Optional proof to bundle with the dispute.

201.description: The frozen job and the dispute.

409.description: The job is already settled or already disputed.

get.summary: The dispute currently open against a job, if any.

post.summary: Resolve the open dispute and release the settlement freeze.
post.description: Resolving does not decide the job — it returns it to its committed condition, which then settles or refunds as before.

200.description: The job and the resolved dispute.

403.description: The key lacks the approve scope.

404.description: No open dispute on this job.

get.summary: One portable decision record: condition, evidence, results, attestation, claims, dispute, timeline.
get.description: Nothing is recomputed at export time, so the dossier can be checked against a replay by a third party.

post.summary: Draft an acceptance condition from what has already settled for this organization.
post.description: A starting point the payer edits and commits — never something that settles on its own.

get.summary: The reproducible settlement receipt: condition, decision, reasons, per-check results, attestation hash.

post.summary: Replay the decision from its attestation and report whether it still matches.

get.summary: Public, signed receipts for settled jobs — newest first.
get.description: A receipt is a portable, EIP-712-signed record of a settlement: decision, subject, commitment hash, receipt hash and signer. The organization, evidence and reasons stay private.

get.summary: One receipt, including its canonical bytes and signature.
Recompute the hash and recover the signer — verification without trusting Elpis.
A subject's reputation, recomputable from its public receipts.
The key that signs public receipts, and the exact EIP-712 domain and types.
A subject's replayable reputation, aggregated over its settlement attestations.

200.description: The reputation score and the signals behind it.

get.summary: Operational counters (settlements, tamper-refusals) and recent structured logs.

post.summary: The same treasury as an MCP tool set (JSON-RPC 2.0), for agents that speak MCP.
post.description: Tools: get_state, list_actions, get_action, evaluate_payment, propose_payment, submit_evidence, approve_payment, draft_condition, settle_job, replay_decision, get_attestation. Each is gated by the key's scope. Policy is not a tool — it is what evaluates the tools' output.

get.summary: Liveness and which execution layer is in use.
